summary.headline: Leela Palaces Q4 FY26: operating revenue up 12% to INR 484 crores and EBITDA up 13% to INR 266 crores, with ADR up 15% offsetting a March occupancy hit.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 484 crores and operating EBITDA rose 13% to INR 266 crores, at a 55% margin, while PAT increased to INR 172 crores from INR 117 crores. Growth was driven by ADR, which rose about 15% to around INR 32,000, while RevPAR grew only 6% as occupancy fell from 78% to 72% after the West Asia conflict disrupted international travel in March. For FY26, operating revenue grew 15% to INR 1,527 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to INR 743 crores at a 49% margin, and PAT reached a record INR 403 crores. Management said April occupancy had recovered to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected for April.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 117 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: City hotels
segments.commentary: Occupancy fell in March on the international, US and UK source-market disruption; management expects city occupancy in mid-70s in FY27. Non-resident covers at city hotels were 54% of the cover mix.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: Described as insulated from the war; management expects a strong rebound in May and June. Resort occupancy guided to mid-60s to late-60s for FY27.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew 15% in FY26 and close to double digits in Q4; banqueting grew more than 10%. Non-resident covers rose about 9-10% in Q4 and about 12% for FY26.

segments.name: Managed hotels / HMA fees
segments.commentary: HMA fees grew double digits in Q4, helped by Hyderabad ramp-up to about 62% occupancy and ADR about 1.24x peer set, plus additional HMA fees from contract terms. FY27 management fees guided to grow double digits.

segments.name: ARQ by The Leela
segments.commentary: Invite-only ultra-luxury club; first club in Bengaluru in FY26, with New Delhi in Q1 FY27, Chennai in Q2 FY27 and Mumbai later in FY27. Initiation fee is INR 45 lakh plus GST; stabilised target is 2,000 members.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 RevPAR growth of high single digit to early double digit in April, and May and June to be very strong; Q1 revenue and EBITDA guided to grow double digit.
FY27 occupancy: city hotels mid-70s, resorts mid-60s to late-60s, blended early 70s.
Net debt to EBITDA to stay around 1.6x in FY27, then fall toward 1.4x and near 1x as new assets ramp; acquisitions could push it slightly higher.
Depreciation to stay around INR 100 crores for the next two to three years, rising only when new hotels open.

Coorg (The Leela Forest Sanctuary): first-year revenue of INR 65-70 crores at about 40% occupancy, with stabilised EBITDA margin of 50-55%; stabilised revenue of INR 165-175 crores in year four including 19 additional villas (capex about INR 38 crores). Rebrand expected end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

Jaisalmer and The Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai to open in FY27. Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore now slated for CY28 (previously FY28), with approvals and funding in place and capex unchanged; Dubai refurbishment to start by end of CY26, handover 1 January 2027 and rebrand 1 January 2028.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio is over 5,200 luxury keys across 24 properties: 15 operational hotels and nine in the pipeline. FY26 keys grew 23% with 966 keys added across Mumbai BKC, Dubai, Jaisalmer and Coorg.
Coorg acquired on 18 March 2026: 71-key all-villa resort on 76 acres, with 25 rooms having heated pools; only about 20 of the 76 acres used so far.
Greenfield projects under construction: Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Sikkim, Agra, Ayodhya and Ranthambore (design, demolition, excavation, piling and structural work underway).
Asset enhancement initiatives (F&B refurbishments, retail, spa, kids club, villa conversions) targeted at about 25% projected yield on cost.
Solar capacity of 2.25 MW commissioned at The Leela Palace Chennai; green energy now 67% of consumption, and power and fuel cost fell to 3% of operating revenue from 3.3% in FY25.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict cut international inbound and outbound travel in March; the international business is roughly 50:50 with domestic in FY26 and has shifted to about 40:60 international to domestic in Q4.
Domestic demand was unaffected; management said April occupancy recovered to last year's levels.
MICE cancellations in March were given credit notes and deferred over six to nine months; management expects a high share to return in coming quarters.
Three weddings originally planned in the Middle East were moved to Leela hotels in March, with more enquiries for April and May.
Expedia and Agoda moved to charging on a gross basis rather than net, which raised sales and marketing and commission costs.
Dubai: asset is 25% owned, with Brookfield holding 75%; management said there is no change in plans and it is focused on operational break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Were March trends sharply weaker and what are April and May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy fell on US and UK source markets while ADR held; April occupancy returned to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected, and May and June strong.

qa_highlights.question: Were there MICE cancellations, and are they deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancellations occurred in March; they were converted to credit notes and deferred over six to nine months, with a high share expected back in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Did Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore slip, and has capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Timing moved from FY28 to CY28 because of approval-linked construction risk; approvals and funding are in place, and capex is unchanged with no cost escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a write-off possibility, that the asset was underwritten on conservative real estate pricing, and that it is evaluating daily.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other costs rise as a percentage of revenue in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to a one-time accrual for new labour code leave encashment and gratuity, plus hiring of value-driver staff; excluding this, payroll rose 8-8.5%, and management expects the ratio to decline.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt to EBITDA trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 1.6x in FY27, falling toward 1.4x and then near 1x as new assets generate EBITDA; acquisitions could push it higher temporarily.

risks_watch: Recovery of international inbound demand from US and UK source markets, which is the segment hit by the West Asia conflict.
Q1 FY27 delivery against the guided high single-digit to early double-digit April RevPAR growth and double-digit May-June performance.
Dubai: a possible impairment if the market stays weak, plus the refurbishment and handover timeline (1 January 2027 handover; 1 January 2028 rebrand).
Q4 cost ratios (employee cost 16.6% of revenue vs 15.9%; other costs up 70 bps), with management expecting them to fall; management did not give exact room, F&B and HMA revenue figures for Q4.
Coorg ramp-up and rebranding, plus ARQ club openings in New Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai.
Depreciation guided flat at about INR 100 crores until new hotels open.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on domestic demand, pricing power and the medium-term outlook, while candid that March international occupancy was hit. Management was less specific on Q4 line-item detail (room, F&B and HMA revenue) and on city-level data, deferring those to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: Our domestic business has not been impacted at all, and whilst some part of our international business has been impacted from a key source market.
The only sub -segment of demand that got impacted because of the war was our international business from our key source markets.

We are looking at an overall stabilized number of 2,000 members, because at that number we feel is the right fit where we can serve them, take care of them, and give them that kind of a luxury experience they have paid for.
The plan remains the same and there is no cost overrun on that front.
